description: For a new two-storey detached house with one basement secondary suite and a building area of 180 m2, we want 9.5 mm gypsum on both sides of the walls and below the floor framing that separate the dwellings. It is continuous and smoke-tight, but we are not offering a rated fire-separation assembly. We are proposing this thinner board in place of the thicker-board secondary-suite option.
known_facts: new detached house with one secondary suite
separating walls and underside of floor framing have 9.5 mm gypsum

missing_info.field: owner or representative contact and property identification
risk assessment, mitigating measures, assumptions and supporting documents
missing_info.why: Alternative-path completeness items; request evidence rather than fabricate a professional conclusion.

gold.departure: The multi-storey main dwelling lacks the required fire-resistance-rated separation, and the proposed 9.5 mm gypsum does not meet the secondary-suite smoke-tight-barrier permission.

should_cite.why: The secondary-suite permission requires at least 12.7 mm gypsum in the specified locations.

must_not_cite.why: The proposed 9.5 mm gypsum is below the stated minimum thickness.

gold.engineering_reason: The house and its secondary suite are within the residential exemption, subject to AHJ special-safety concerns; no Part 4 structural work is described.
